## Edge cases

- **No `jq`:** New Python paths must work without `jq`.
- **Malformed JSON:** Skip bad JSONL or NDJSON rows where bash previously ignored parser failures.
- **Missing round roots:** Review detail returns empty output for missing or unreadable roots, except the no-rounds message for a readable root with no completed rounds.
- **Partial round artifacts:** Render available counts and labels. Do not fail final reports.
- **Design security OOS:** Preserve subtraction of security OOS items from design OOS accepted or rejected counts.
- **Panel-manifest snapshots:** Design round-meta must still materialize `panel-manifest.ndjson` from the round-local slots file or the session-root fallback.
- **Token ledger windows:** Keep inclusive `[start_s, end_s]` attribution for vendor cost rows.
- **Gantt overlap:** Since #4546 overlaps this area, keep the current Gantt text stable unless tests prove a required difference.
- **Run-log GC:** Never mutate non-dry-run state when the tree is dirty, the branch is not `main`, or `larch-logs/` is missing.
- **Status:** A failed probe must still produce a complete KV set with conservative values.

## Failure modes when non-trivial

- **Retired-script lint failures:** Adding deleted paths to `migrated-scripts.tsv` will make stale prose references fail. Update docs, tests, and allowlists in the same change.
- **Hidden test dependencies:** Bash harnesses may copy or stub retired scripts. Remove those fixtures or convert them to Python CLI stubs.
- **Behavior drift in markdown tables:** The review phase detail output is regression-sensitive. Use golden-ish assertions for headings, rows, totals, Gantt header, and sentinel-free markdown.
- **GC external side effects:** Non-dry-run GC creates branches, commits, pushes, and PRs. Tests must stub external commands and run in temp repos.
- **Quiet stream drift:** `gc-run-logs run` and `status check` must keep KV output parseable. Avoid raw diagnostics on stdout.
- **Module naming mismatch:** The discussion says `agent.py`, but the repo uses `python/agents.py`. Implement in `python/agents.py` and register `status check` there.

- Run focused Python tests:

- Run CLI smoke checks:
  - `python3 python/cli.py progress render-phase-detail --rounds-root <fixture> --skill implement`
  - `python3 python/cli.py render findings-view <fixture-run-dir> all`
  - `python3 python/cli.py status check`
  - `python3 python/cli.py gc-run-logs run --dry-run --older-than 90` in a temp repo fixture.
- Run migration checks:
  - `make lint-retired-scripts`
  - `python3 python/cli.py --help` and confirm new verbs appear.
- Run required repo checks:
  - `make py-lint`
  - `make py-test`
  - `make lint`
- If only the focused test subset is practical during implementation, document skipped full checks and why.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# render-findings-view.sh — Render a dropped markdown view from review-findings-full.jsonl.
     3	# Usage: render-findings-view.sh <run-dir> [accepted|rejected|oos|all]
     4	# Outputs the requested view to stdout. Exits 1 when the jsonl is absent.
     5	
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	
     8	usage() {
     9	    printf 'Usage: render-findings-view.sh <larch-logs/implement/RUN_ID/> [accepted|rejected|oos|all]\n' >&2
    10	    exit 1
    11	}
    12	
    13	[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage
    14	RUN_DIR="$1"
    15	VIEW="${2:-all}"
    16	
    17	JSONL="$RUN_DIR/review-findings-full.jsonl"
    18	if [ ! -f "$JSONL" ]; then
    19	    printf 'render-findings-view.sh: review-findings-full.jsonl not found in %s\n' "$RUN_DIR" >&2
    20	    exit 1
    21	fi
    22	
    23	case "$VIEW" in
    24	    accepted|rejected|oos|all) ;;
    25	    *) printf 'render-findings-view.sh: unknown view %s (accepted|rejected|oos|all)\n' "$VIEW" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    26	esac
    27	
    28	# Build jq outcome filter
    29	if [ "$VIEW" = "all" ]; then
    30	    OUTCOME_FILTER='true'
    31	elif [ "$VIEW" = "oos" ]; then
    32	    OUTCOME_FILTER='.outcome == "out_of_scope"'
    33	else
    34	    OUTCOME_FILTER=".outcome == \"$VIEW\""
    35	fi
    36	
    37	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'render-findings-view.sh: jq is required\n' >&2; exit 1; }
    38	
    39	jq -r --arg view "$VIEW" "
    40	select($OUTCOME_FILTER) |
    41	\"### FINDING (\" + .outcome + \") round-\" + (.round_num | tostring) + \"\\n\" +
    42	(.prose_body // \"(no prose body)\") + \"\\n\"
    43	" "$JSONL"

    33	_parse_tally_md() {
    34	    local file="$1"
    35	    awk -F'|' '
    36	        function trim(s) { gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
    37	        /^## Findings/ { in_findings=1; next }
    38	        /^## / && in_findings { in_findings=0 }
    39	        in_findings && NF >= 4 {
    40	            item=trim($2)

    43	                result=trim($(NF-2))

    98	import sys

   124	    case "$source" in
   125	        md)
   126	            while IFS=$'\t' read -r id result || [[ -n "$id" ]]; do

   140	                function trim(s) { gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
   141	                /^## Findings/ { in_findings = 1; next }

   154	            ;;
   155	        tsv)
   156	            while IFS=$'\t' read -r id result || [[ -n "$id" ]]; do
   157	                [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
   158	                [[ "$id" =~ ^OOS_[0-9A-Za-z_]+$ ]] || continue
   159	                [[ -n "$result" ]] || continue

   167	                        esac
   168	                    fi
   169	                fi
   170	                rm -f "$block_file"
   171	            done < <(awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 && $1 ~ /^OOS_/ { print $1 "\t" $3 }' \
   172	                "$round_dir/findings-classification.tsv" 2>/dev/null)
   173	            ;;
   174	    esac
   175	    if (( OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT < 0 )); then OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT=0; fi
   176	    if (( OOS_REJECTED_COUNT < 0 )); then OOS_REJECTED_COUNT=0; fi
   177	}

   182	_tsv_counts=""

    15	# round by timestamp window ([round.start_s, round.end_s]) and priced via
    16	# python token cost. It excludes main-agent Claude, so it is strictly the vendor
    17	# spend for that round and is therefore less than the run-total Cost line in the

   474	def _progress_derived_label(output: str) -> str:
   475	    core = _progress_core_from_output(output)

   483	    match = re.match(rf"^({vendor_match})-specialist-(.+)$", core)
   484	    if match:
   485	        return f"{match.group(1)}/{match.group(2)}"
   486	    match = re.match(rf"^({vendor_match})-generalist$", core)
   487	    if match:
   488	        return f"{match.group(1)}/generalist"
   489	    if core.startswith("dyn-"):
   490	        return f"dynamic/{core[4:]}"
   491	    match = re.match(rf"^({vendor_match})-(.*)$", core)
   492	    if match:

   494	        return f"{match.group(1)}/{arch}"

   541	    window_end_s: int,
   542	    label_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,

   548	    try:

   550	    except OSError:

   552	    rows: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
   553	    for line in lines:
   554	        cols = line.split("\t")
   555	        if len(cols) < TIMING_VENDOR_MIN_COLS or cols[0] != "v1" or cols[1] != "vendor":
   556	            continue
   557	        status = cols[TIMING_VENDOR_STATUS_COL]

   559	            continue
   560	        try:
   561	            start_s = int(cols[TIMING_VENDOR_START_COL])
   562	            end_s = int(cols[TIMING_VENDOR_END_COL])
   563	        except ValueError:
   564	            continue
   565	        if end_s <= window_start_s or start_s >= window_end_s:
   566	            continue
   567	        clamped_start = max(start_s, window_start_s)
   568	        clamped_end = min(end_s, window_end_s)
   569	        if clamped_end <= clamped_start:
   570	            continue
   571	        output = cols[TIMING_VENDOR_OUTPUT_COL] if len(cols) > TIMING_VENDOR_OUTPUT_COL else ""
   572	        kind = cols[TIMING_VENDOR_KIND_COL]
   573	        if skip_ci and _is_ci_gantt_row(kind, output):
   574	            continue
   575	        label = _derive_progress_label(output, cols[TIMING_VENDOR_VENDOR_COL], kind, label_map)
   576	        rows.append((clamped_start, clamped_end, label))
   577	    rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row[0], row[1], row[2]))
   578	    return [GanttRow(label, start_s, end_s) for start_s, end_s, label in rows[:PROGRESS_GANTT_ROW_CAP]]

    67	def extract_markdown_section(text: str, start_header: str, end_headers: Sequence[str] = _FINDINGS_END_HEADERS) -> str:
    68	    """Return a fenced-aware markdown section body without the start header."""
    69	    lines = text.splitlines()
    70	    in_section = False
    71	    in_fence = False
    72	    out: list[str] = []
    73	    end_set = set(end_headers)
    74	    for line in lines:
    75	        if re.match(r"^[ \t]*```", line):
    76	            if in_section:
    77	                out.append(line)
    78	            in_fence = not in_fence
    79	            continue
    80	        if in_fence:
    81	            if in_section:
    82	                out.append(line)
    83	            continue
    84	        if not in_section:
    85	            if line == start_header:
    86	                in_section = True
    87	            continue
    88	        if line.startswith("## ") or line in end_set:
    89	            break
    90	        out.append(line)
    91	    return "\n".join(out)

    94	def strip_outer_blank_lines(text: str) -> str:
    95	    """Trim only leading and trailing blank lines."""
    96	    lines = text.splitlines()
    97	    start = 0
    98	    end = len(lines)
    99	    while start < end and not lines[start].strip():
   100	        start += 1
   101	    while end > start and not lines[end - 1].strip():
   102	        end -= 1
   103	    return "\n".join(lines[start:end])

   107	    """Extract a section and flatten non-empty lines into one metadata value."""
   108	    body = strip_outer_blank_lines(extract_markdown_section(text, header))

   111	    values: list[str] = []
   112	    for line in body.splitlines():
   113	        value = re.sub(r"^[ \t]*[-*][ \t]*", "", line)

   124	    text = strip_outer_blank_lines(findings_text)
   125	    if not text:
   126	        return []
   127	    items: list[str] = []
   128	    current: list[str] = []
   129	    mode = ""

   133	    def emit_current() -> None:
   134	        nonlocal current
   135	        item = strip_outer_blank_lines("\n".join(current))
   136	        if item:
   137	            items.append(item)
   138	        current = []

   140	    for line in text.splitlines():
   141	        if re.match(r"^```", line):

   143	            current.append(line)
   144	            continue
   145	        if in_fence:
   146	            current.append(line)
   147	            continue
   148	        if re.match(r"^####\s+subquestion\s+[0-9]+", line, re.IGNORECASE):
   149	            emit_current()

   156	        if not mode:
   157	            if is_numbered:
   158	                mode = "numbered"
   159	                current = [line]

   161	                continue
   162	            if is_bulleted:
   163	                mode = "bulleted"

   166	                continue
   167	            if line.strip():
   168	                mode = "paragraph"
   169	                current = [line]

   171	        if not current and (is_numbered or is_bulleted):
   172	            mode = "numbered" if is_numbered else "bulleted"
   173	            current = [line]

   175	            continue

---\n\nApply accepted review findings as code fixes. Internal sub-skill invoked by `/review` in diff mode and by `/implement` Step 5; not a standalone user entry point. It dispatches Codex, Cursor, then a Claude subagent fallback to apply voted-in suggestions directly, with pre-dispatch submodule finding scrubbing and post-dispatch submodule revert checks. `--findings-file` is required; `--session-env` and `--review-tmpdir` are optional.\n\n### `/set-up-forked-open-source-repo`\n\n**Arguments**: `--upstream <owner/repo> --fork <owner/repo> [--mirror-confirmed] [--init-submodules]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/set-up-forked-open-source-repo/SKILL.md`](../skills/set-up-forked-open-source-repo/SKILL.md)\n\nConfigure the current checkout for upstream/fork OSS contribution. The skill verifies that the fork exists on GitHub and that its immediate parent is the declared upstream, probes both repositories' `refs/heads/main`, optionally performs a destructive fork sync of branches and tags after explicit confirmation, then rewires local remotes so `origin` points at the fork and `upstream` points at upstream. It disables upstream pushes with an invalid-scheme push URL, fetches `origin`, sets `main` to track `origin/main`, and fast-forwards only from a clean `main` checkout.\n\nThe workflow is intentionally single-clone (per-clone single-flight lock; multiple clones may run concurrently) and supports any GitHub-compatible host, with github.com as the default. It refuses dirty linked worktrees, in-progress git operations in any linked worktree, missing local `main`, non-`main` checkouts, local `main` ahead of `origin/main`, diverged local/remote `main`, ambiguous remote layouts, non-parseable / mixed-host URLs, duplicate fork remotes, multi-fetch URL remotes, and multi-push URL remotes. If the fork is missing, it prints fork-creation instructions and exits without local mutation. `--init-submodules` is opt-in; default runs ignore submodules.\n\n### `/status`\n\n**Arguments**: *(none)*\n\n**Source**: [`skills/status/SKILL.md`](../skills/status/SKILL.md)\n\nPrint the current larch version and health status of external vendor tools (Codex and Cursor). Uses the same probe machinery as `/implement` Step 0: `agent check-reviewers` for binary/runtime probes, then `python3 python/cli.py agent degraded-tools-gate` to classify each vendor as `ok`, `binary-missing`, or `probe-failed`. Reports whether the session would run degraded (reduced panel or Claude-only fallback).\n\n### `/upgrade-larch`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--run-id <ID>]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/upgrade-larch/SKILL.md`](../skills/upgrade-larch/SKILL.md)\n\nUpgrade the larch plugin to the latest version. Targets the standard sparse GitHub install (`claude plugin marketplace add character-ai/larch --sparse .claude-plugin agents docs hooks python scripts skills`): the skill refreshes the sparse marketplace checkout in place when possible, repairs legacy full clones or stale sparse cones with a sparse re-add, then reinstalls when either a newer release or a same-version cone repair is needed. It also cleans dev/test files and dropped dev top-level directories from the installed cache as part of the run, including on the already-latest path. The optional `--run-id <ID>` overrides the auto-generated run identifier. Contributors using a local checkout (`claude --plugin-dir .` or `claude plugin marketplace add .`) should `git pull` instead. Delegates to `python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py\" upgrade-larch run`; on success the user is told to restart Claude Code when a new version was installed or the sparse cone was reconciled.\n\n## Aliases\n\n\n--- external reviewers ---\n# External Agents\n\n## Availability Checks\n\nAt the start of each skill, a binary check plus runtime probe (`python/cli.py agent check-reviewers` via `session-setup.sh --check-reviewers`) determines which external tools are usable:\n\n- If **Codex** is unavailable (binary not on `PATH`, or its runtime auth/quota probe fails), a warning is printed\n- If **Cursor** is unavailable (same two failure modes), a warning is printed\n\n**Degraded-tools gate (issue #3207).** Beyond the warning, every skill that uses external tools (`/design`, `/implement`, `/review`, `/research`) runs the **Degraded-tools gate** in Step 0 (`python3 python/cli.py agent degraded-tools-gate`; procedure in `skills/shared/external-reviewers.md`). When either tool is unavailable, the gate presents an explanation (what is down, why — binary-missing vs runtime-probe-failed — and the degradation to expect). On an **interactive** run, `AskUserQuestion` fires only when **both** tools are down (`BOTH_DOWN` is not exactly `false`); when exactly one tool is down (`BOTH_DOWN=false`), the explanation is printed as a notice and the run proceeds automatically without prompting. Non-interactive / autonomous runs (cron, `claude -p`, eval) auto-proceed degraded with the explanation logged, so automation is never blocked.\n\n**Codex auth scope.** Covered Codex paths prefer a live non-whitespace `OPENAI_API_KEY` through per-invocation `-c` provider overrides; unset, empty, or whitespace-only falls back to `codex login` / `~/.codex/auth.json`. The merged inventory is: `python/cli.py agent launch-review --tool codex`, `python/cli.py agent launch-codex-ci`, `agent launch-codex-implement`, the Codex health probe in `python/cli.py agent check-reviewers`, `python/cli.py review-and-fix apply-findings`, `python/cli.py agent launch-codex-exec`, `/research` Codex research lanes, `/research` validation lane, shared Codex voter/judge fences, `python/cli.py checks lint-fix`, and `python/cli.py agent run-negotiation-round`.\n\n## Trust boundary (filesystem access)\n\n## Launching External Reviewers\n\nExternal reviewers are launched via `python3 python/cli.py agent run-external-agent`, which provides:\n\n- **Timeout enforcement** — Kills the process after a configurable timeout\n- **Sentinel file creation** — Writes a `.done` file containing the exit code when the process completes\n- **Output capture** — two patterns, opt-in per invocation:\n  - **stdout capture under `--capture-stdout`** — when the reviewer writes its results to stdout, pass `--capture-stdout` and the wrapper redirects the tool's stdout/stderr to `--output`. Invoke them as `/<name>` (or the fully-qualified `/larch:<name>`) in any repository with larch loaded.\n- **Aliases** are public skills generated by [`/alias`](#alias) that forward to an existing skill with preset flags; they ship under `skills/` and are listed in their own section.\n- **Private skills** are dev-only (`.claude/skills/`). They are **not** exported by the plugin and run only inside this larch source tree.\n\nThe skill set documented here matches the skills in the repository. Each entry lists invocation arguments, the canonical `SKILL.md` source, and behavior.\n\n## Public skills\n\n- [`/alias`](#alias)\n- [`/block-issue`](#block-issue)\n- [`/bug`](#bug)\n- [`/cleanup`](#cleanup)\n- [`/design`](#design)\n- [`/fluff-analysis`](#fluff-analysis)\n- [`/gc-run-logs`](#gc-run-logs)\n- [`/implement`](#implement)\n- [`/issue`](#issue)\n- [`/pause`](#pause)\n- [`/report-tokens`](#report-tokens)\n- [`/research`](#research)\n- [`/review`](#review)\n- [`/review-and-fix`](#review-and-fix)\n- [`/set-up-forked-open-source-repo`](#set-up-forked-open-source-repo)\n- [`/status`](#status)\n- [`/upgrade-larch`](#upgrade-larch)\n\n### `/alias`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--merge] [--private] <alias-name> <target-skill> [preset-flags...]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/alias/SKILL.md`](../skills/alias/SKILL.md)\n\nCreate an alias for a larch skill with preset flags. Delegates to `/implement` for the full pipeline per `skills/alias/SKILL.md` (code review, PR, CI). Versioning is `/release` or manual `release` only (Phase 1 #3364). `--merge` also merges the PR.\n\n**Target directory** is auto-resolved: inside a Claude plugin source repo (detected by the two-file predicate `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` AND `skills/implement/SKILL.md` at the git repo root), the alias is generated under `skills/<alias-name>/SKILL.md` (exported plugin skill, ships with the plugin); anywhere else, it's generated under `.claude/skills/<alias-name>/SKILL.md` (dev-only repo-private). `--private` forces `.claude/skills/<alias-name>/` even inside a plugin repo (escape hatch); in non-plugin repos it's a no-op.\n\nExample (in a plugin repo): `/alias i implement --merge` creates `<repo-root>/skills/i/SKILL.md` so that `/i <issue-N>` forwards to `/implement --merge <issue-N>` with any additional preset flags captured in the alias body.\n\nExample with `--private` or in a consumer repo: `/alias i implement --merge` creates `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/i/SKILL.md` (dev-only).\n\n### `/block-issue`\n\n**Arguments**: `<ISSUE_A> <ISSUE_B> [--repo owner/name]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/block-issue/SKILL.md`](../skills/block-issue/SKILL.md)\n\nExpress a native GitHub blocked-by relationship between two issues using the `addBlockedBy` GraphQL mutation. ISSUE_A is marked as blocked by ISSUE_B. Repo is auto-detected from `gh repo view` when `--repo` is omitted. Verifies the relationship was recorded before confirming.\n\n### `/bug`\n\n**Arguments**: `<bug description>`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/bug/SKILL.md`](../skills/bug/SKILL.md)\n\nInvestigate a user-described bug inline, compose a detailed issue body, then delegate creation to `/issue` with dedup enabled. This skill is for issue filing only: it reads the repo with `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` and safe read-only `Bash`, never edits it, and writes scratch artifacts only under a `/tmp` `$BUG_TMPDIR`. The whole `$ARGUMENTS` string is the bug description; the skill takes no flags. If the report looks like a **security vulnerability** (or might be), it aborts before filing and points at `SECURITY.md` responsible disclosure. The composed body uses a fixed ten-heading template (Summary, Original report, Reproduction scenario, Expected, Observed, Root cause analysis, Evidence, Affected files, Suggested fix(es), Open questions) and is sanitized before write.\n\n### `/cleanup`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--run-id <ID>]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/cleanup/SKILL.md`](../skills/cleanup/SKILL.md)\n\nRemove stale larch session temp directories from `~/.cache/larch/sessions/` and `/tmp` by age (`LARCH_CLEANUP_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 7). Directories are removed only when no file within the bounded `find -maxdepth 5` scan is newer than the cutoff; a directory with fresh deep activity (≤ 5 levels) is retained even when its top-level mtime is old. Matching loose `/tmp` files are removed by top-level age and pattern match. Reaps dangling `current-design-env-*.sh` symlinks. Always runnable — reports `SESSION_COUNT` for visibility but does not abort when multiple Claude sessions are active. The optional `--run-id <ID>` overrides the auto-generated run identifier.\n\n### `/design`\n\n**Arguments**: `[-p|--partition] [--brainstorm] [--per-round-approval] [--skip-approve|-s] [--no-dedup] [--run-id <ID>] <issue-N | feature description>`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/design/SKILL.md`](../skills/design/SKILL.md)\n\nDesign an implementation plan with the mechanical plan-review panel. `/design` uses a single direct-drafting flow: Step 2a writes sentinel artifacts, Step 2b drafts the plan from direct codebase inspection, and Step 3 runs the full plan-review panel. `-p`/`--partition` requests the Step 2b.5 partition/break-up flow when no plan-size threshold trips; optional `--brainstorm` runs Step 1d.5 ideation before the Step 1d.7 outline-approval gate (Gate A re-entry only post-plan); Gate B auto-applies accepted findings by default, `--per-round-approval` restores the explicit per-round prompt (the former manual flag is rejected), and `--skip-approve`/`-s` auto-approves the Step 1d.7 outline and Gate C final plan (no other prompts are skipped) — see `skills/design/references/flags.md`. Internal-only flags also live there. A bare feature description (no `<issue-N>`) creates an issue first. After final approval, **Step 5b** may file accepted non-security OOS items via `/larch:issue` (`[OOS]` prefix) before **Step 5c** writes the `larch:plan` block to the issue; **Step 6** removes the design tmpdir.\n\n### `/fluff-analysis`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--include-in-progress] [--cutoff ISO8601] [--since-version X.Y.Z] [--min-group N] [--log-root DIR] [--out FILE]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/fluff-analysis/SKILL.md`](../skills/fluff-analysis/SKILL.md)\n\nCharacterize review **fluff** — suggestions that are *not accepted* (rejected or deferred to Out-of-Scope) or *accepted-but-low-value* — from committed `larch-logs/design/*/` and `larch-logs/implement/*/` run directories in the current repository. The analyzer normalizes every review finding (outcome, reviewer/voter severity, multi-label semantic tags) and prints a markdown report: acceptance baselines, low-acceptance semantic groups (distinguishing reject-heavy true fluff from OOS-heavy valid-but-deferred), a testing breakdown, severity/quality/uncertain correlations, reviewer-lane splits, an accepted-but-low-value proxy, optional pre/post comparison (`--cutoff` by timestamp or `--since-version` by `manifest.json.larch_version`), and data-driven recommendations. Keyword tags are directional; severity and outcome cuts are exact. `--include-in-progress` additionally reads un-flushed `/design` session temp dirs (racy snapshot, off by default; tunable with `--sessions-dir` / `--inprogress-since`). `--min-group N` sets the minimum findings for a semantic group to appear (default 20). `--out FILE` writes the report to a file instead of stdout. This is the standing tool behind `[Analysis Report]` issues; re-run it as the corpus grows to track whether necessity-gate changes (`skills/shared/review-acceptance-rubric.md`) move acceptance and findings-per-run. Skill-local Python is not covered by `make py-lint` (scoped to `python/`).\n\n### `/gc-run-logs`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--older-than DAYS] [--delete] [--dry-run]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/gc-run-logs/SKILL.md`](../skills/gc-run-logs/SKILL.md)\n\nAge-based retention policy for committed `larch-logs/` run directories (`design/`, `implement/`, `review/`). Slims qualifying run dirs (older than `--older-than DAYS`, default 90) to the consumer-core keep set: `manifest.json`, `final-summary.md`, token/timing reports, findings, and execution issues. All other files and subdirectories (round forensics, aggregator artifacts, voter outputs) are removed. `--delete` fully removes qualifying dirs instead of slimming; content remains recoverable via git history. `--dry-run` previews the plan without changes. Dirs with a `pause-state.txt`, a `gc-slimmed` marker, or no resolvable run date are skipped. Creates a log-only PR for operator review and merge; never runs implicitly and never merges on the operator's behalf.\n\n### `/implement`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--merge] [--forked] [--draft] [--no-admin-fallback] [--no-logs-commit] [--coder <claude|codex|cursor>] [--run-id <ID>] [--emergency] [--self-review] <issue-N>`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/implement/SKILL.md`](../skills/implement/SKILL.md) · [Diagram](../skills/implement/diagram.svg)\n\nFull implementation workflow spanning design through PR merge. Preflight consumes the **positional** GitHub `<issue-N>` after `/design` has written `larch:plan` into that issue's body. Step 5 invokes `review-and-fix step5`, which uses a fixed round cap of **5** (hard ceiling), does **not** forward `--panel` on the public argv, and applies the panel only inside `review-and-fix CLI` → `review core`: a **3-judge panel on every round** (Claude opus + Codex + Cursor when both vendors are available; shrink-not-backfill drops an unavailable external instead of replacing it), with the **review panel** and **specialists per vendor** (plus optional dynamic archetypes). `--merge` enables CI+merge; `--forked` is mutually exclusive with `--merge`. `--emergency` bypasses plan-block presence / plan-adequacy audit / clarify-state pending gates with loud warnings and forces `coder=claude` (mutually exclusive with `--draft`; compatible with `--merge`); default is off. `--self-review` skips the external review panel and has the main agent perform a thorough inline self-review at Step 5 instead. Preflight audit refusal exits **3** (distinct from flag/plan hard errors, which exit **2**).\n\n### `/issue`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--input-file FILE] [--intra-batch-deps-file FILE] [--blocked-by-issue N] [--title-prefix PREFIX] [--label LABEL]... [--body-file FILE] [--dry-run] [--no-dedup] [--no-dep-llm] [--sentinel-file PATH] [<issue description or title>]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/issue/SKILL.md`](../skills/issue/SKILL.md)\n\nCreate one or more GitHub issues with LLM-based semantic duplicate detection. Supports single mode (free-form description) and batch mode (`--input-file`). 2-phase dedup against open + recently-closed issues (default 90-day window). `--no-dedup` skips the entire dedup + dependency analysis pipeline and creates all items directly — useful for archival issues (e.g., `/research` reports) where each run produces genuinely different content. `--no-dep-llm` keeps dedup but skips the LLM dependency-detection pass. `--title-prefix`, `--label`, `--body-file`, `--blocked-by-issue`, `--intra-batch-deps-file`, and `--sentinel-file` are used primarily by calling skills (`/design` Step 5b, `/implement` Step 9a.1, `/bug`) that file issues in batch or wire dependencies.\n\n**Default-on inter-issue blocker-dependency analysis** (issue #546): unless `--no-dedup` is set, every invocation analyzes the new item(s) against existing OPEN issues and applies hard GitHub-native blocker dependencies via the Issue Dependencies REST API on detected pairs (merge-conflict risk or \"must land first\"). Hard-fail with retries (3 tries, 10s/30s sleeps); on retry exhaustion the failed item is rolled back (orphan close) — when multiple items are processed, unrelated items continue — and the run exits non-zero if any item failed, yielding a clean \"create-then-close\" recovery rather than a dangling issue with missing dependency wiring.\n\n### `/pause`\n\n**Arguments**: *(none)*\n\n**Source**: [`skills/pause/SKILL.md`](../skills/pause/SKILL.md)\n\nPause a live `/design` session on the current Claude PID. The skill sources the\ncurrent design session env, publishes the tmpdir with\n`design-log-publish.sh --reason pause`, writes a `larch:design-pause` marker in\nthe issue body, and exits. Re-running `/design <issue>` detects that marker in\nStep 0b, restores the tmpdir, deletes the marker, and resumes at the first\nincomplete step. If no live `/design` env is present, it reports that there is\nnothing to pause and exits successfully.\n\n### `/report-tokens`\n\n**Arguments**: `--skill <design|implement> [--no-issue] [--no-plot] [--run-id <ID>]`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/report-tokens/SKILL.md`](../skills/report-tokens/SKILL.md)\n\nAnalyze structured token reports from committed `larch-logs/<skill>/*/` run directories in the current larch repository. The skill requires `--skill=design|implement`, prices runs through `python/report_tokens_cost.py`, writes a durable `Cache JSON:` NDJSON snapshot under a temp directory, optionally plots cost-over-time PNGs (`--no-plot` skips), and optionally posts a skill-prefixed GitHub issue (`--no-issue` skips). The optional `--run-id <ID>` is consumed by the orchestrator and not forwarded to the CLI. Both skills use one aggregate graph and one per-day table set. Filed issues omit raw per-issue JSON and the removed reported-vs-estimated comparison. Dollar values are observability estimates, not billing truth; rates are printed and can be overridden with environment variables.\n\n### `/research`\n\n**Arguments**: `[--no-issue] <research question or topic>`\n\n**Source**: [`skills/research/SKILL.md`](../skills/research/SKILL.md) · [Diagram](../skills/research/diagram.svg)\n\nCollaborative best-effort read-only research with a fixed-shape topology. The research phase always runs a planner pre-pass that decomposes `RESEARCH_QUESTION` into focused subquestions, then the [Codex-first lanes](topology.md#research.lanes) listed in the research skill (architecture / edge cases / external comparisons / security) with a per-lane Claude `Agent` fallback when Codex is unavailable. The validation phase runs the [panel](topology.md#research.validation_panel) described in [Review Agents](review-agents.md), with Claude fallbacks when an external tool is unavailable. Cursor pattern; canonical examples at `skills/review/SKILL.md:146-148, 177-179`.\n  - **tool-managed output path** — when the reviewer takes its own output-path argument (e.g., Codex's `--output-last-message`), omit `--capture-stdout`; the wrapper does not capture stdout and the reviewer writes results directly to the file. 1	# Python Migration Playbook (sh-to-py)
     2	
     3	This document describes how to port a bash script domain into the larch Python
     4	runtime and retire the old bash surface. Every subsequent sh-to-py issue follows
     5	this recipe.
     6	
     7	## Decision log
     8	
     9	- **No shims for migration cutover**: when retiring a bash domain or making a voluntary port, consumers call `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py" <domain> <verb> [args...]` directly. Do not add intermediate `.sh` forwarding stubs as migration cutover aids. Delete retired bash per recipe steps 4-6. This prohibition does not forbid forward-looking thin glue wrappers governed by the Python-first policy: thin environment-plus-`cli.py` delegation wrappers, Claude Code hooks, and pre-commit or CI glue.
    10	- **Python-first for new scripts**: new larch script logic lives in `python/` behind `python3 python/cli.py`. Bash is allowed only for thin environment-plus-`cli.py` delegation wrappers, Claude Code hooks, and pre-commit or CI glue. This complements [recipe step 4](#per-domain-migration-recipe), **Cut ALL consumers to direct `cli.py` calls**, so migration and voluntary-port cutover keep direct `cli.py` calls while forward-looking glue-wrapper permissions stay separate. See [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [`.claude/rules/python-first-scripts.md`](../.claude/rules/python-first-scripts.md).
    11	- **Hard cutover**: once a domain is registered in `cli.py`, all consumers (skills, docs, Makefile, CI) are repointed in the same commit. No `LARCH_*_IMPL`-style selectors.
    12	- **Hooks stay bash**: Claude Code hooks remain bash pending a separate overhaul.
    13	- **Flat layout**: all Python modules live directly under `python/` (no sub-packages).
    14	- **Stdlib-only, Python ≥ 3.11**: the runtime must not import third-party packages; dev/CI linters (ruff, pyright, pylint) and pytest are installed separately via requirements files.
    15	- **`cli.py` is the canonical entrypoint** for all external consumers. Adopted modules MAY keep `if __name__ == "__main__":` blocks as compatibility pass-throughs; `cli.py` becomes canonical via consumer cutover + docs + lint, not by disabling module execution.
    16	- **fd-3 via `quiet_init`/`contract_stream`/`emit_kv`**: KV output intended for the .md orchestrator always goes to the contract stream (fd 3 after `quiet_init`, else stdout). Post-quiet human diagnostics go through `BreadcrumbWriter` (never raw `print(file=sys.stderr)` after `quiet_init`).
    17	
    18	- **G1 review pipeline port (#3692)**: `python/review_pipeline.py` owns `gather-context`, `dispatch-panel`, `collect-findings`, `check-reviewer-failure-threshold`, `core`, and `reviewer-prune` in-process. `python/review_aggregate.py`, `python/review_tally.py`, and `python/compose_review.py` remain CLI façades for the retained aggregate/tally/emit/compose/log-phase shell bodies under `python/legacy_review_shell/`.
    19	
    20	- **C3a1 plan-review CLI façade (#3680)**: `python/plan_review.py` and `python/plan_review_panel.py` register the shipped `plan-review` verbs but delegate loop, emit/finalize/preview, state, timing, Gate B dedup, panel dispatch, and voter dispatch to gzip-embedded retired bash via `_run_legacy()` / `_materialize_legacy_root()`. The `tally` verb is ported in-process to `python/plan_review_tally.py` (the gzip-embedded `tally-plan-review.sh` body is retained for contract tests but no longer executed). Treat the remaining delegated Python entry points as CLI entrypoints and contract relays, not as the implementation authority for Step 3 loop bodies, panel dispatch, or voter dispatch until a follow-up issue ports them in-process. Operator docs should name `python/cli.py plan-review <verb>` (with an explicit delegation note where relevant) rather than deleted script paths.
    21	
    22	## Per-domain migration recipe
    23	
    24	1. **Port functions** into a new or existing `python/<module>.py`. Keep the module
    25	   stdlib-only; rely on `proc.py` for subprocess calls, `logging_util.py` for
    26	   observability, and `config.py` for tunables.
    27	
    28	2. **Register CLI subcommands** — add a `("<domain>", "<verb>"): ("<module>", "main")`
    29	   entry to `_REGISTRY` in `python/cli.py`. Keep top-level imports in `cli.py`
    30	   limited to `argparse`, `importlib`, and `sys`.
    31	
    32	3. **Write colocated pytest** in `python/test_<module>.py`. Subprocess cases derive
    33	   the CLI path from `Path(__file__).with_name("cli.py")`. Cover the fd-3 contract,
    34	   quiet mode behavior, and edge cases. Do NOT include retired-path literals in test
    35	   fixtures; build paths at runtime instead.
    36	
    37	4. **Cut ALL consumers to direct `cli.py` calls** — skill `.md` files, docs, Makefile
    38	   targets, CI workflow steps, and any bash helper that invoked the old script. Change
    39	   every `scripts/old-script.sh` or `python/old_module.py` invocation to
    40	   `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py" <domain> <verb> [args...]`.
    41	   Bash callers should derive the plugin root from their local script directory
    42	   first (falling back to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`) so direct execution from a
    43	   checkout does not depend on a prehydrated environment variable.
    44	
    45	5. **Run retargeted `test-*.sh` harnesses once as a parity gate** — after consumer
    46	   cutover, confirm the bash integration harnesses still pass against the new CLI
    47	   surface before deleting the old bash files.
    48	
    49	6. **Delete bash script + harness + `.md` siblings** — remove the old
    50	   `.sh`, `.md`, and test harness files. Do not leave stubs.
    51	
    52	7. **Append to manifest** — add the deleted paths to `python/migrated-scripts.tsv`
    53	   (full repo-relative path in column 1, `#<issue>` in column 2). This is how
    54	   `make lint-retired-scripts` knows what to check for lingering references.
    55	
    56	8. **`make lint-retired-scripts`** — run (or let CI run) `make lint-retired-scripts`
    57	   to confirm no tracked file still references any of the retired paths.
    58	
    59	## Manifest format
    60	
    61	`python/migrated-scripts.tsv` — tab-separated, `path<TAB>retired_by`:
    62	
    63	```
    64	# Retired script manifest for the sh-to-py migration.
    65	# Format: path<TAB>retired_by
    66	scripts/old-helper.sh    #1234
    67	```
    68	
    69	Rules:
    70	
    71	- **Path-precise references plus scoped dev-skill basenames.** The linter matches
    72	  the full repo-relative manifest path everywhere and same-directory
    73	  `$SCRIPT_DIR/<basename>.sh` / `${SCRIPT_DIR}/<basename>.sh` forms derived from
    74	  that manifest path. It also matches bare basenames only in same-directory
    75	  `.claude/skills/**/*.md` dev-skill docs when no live sibling `.sh` exists.
    76	  Repo-wide bare basenames outside that scoped branch are not matched, so a live
    77	  file at `other/path/run-analysis.sh` will not be flagged for a retired path at
    78	  `scripts/old/run-analysis.sh`.
    79	- Retired path references are deletion blockers whenever they match the manifest
    80	  path or same-directory invocation forms. Comment and prose references are
    81	  scanned the same way as code unless they fall under the exclusions below.
    82	- Exclusions from scanning: any file under a `larch-logs/` path segment,
    83	  `CHANGELOG.md`, and the manifest file itself are never scanned.
    84	- **Do NOT write retired-path literals in test fixtures.** Build fixture paths
    85	  programmatically at runtime so tests remain valid if the manifest changes.
    86	
    87	## Lint invocation
    88	
    89	```bash
    90	# Check for stale references to retired paths.
    91	make lint-retired-scripts
    92	```
    93	
    94	Wired into `make lint` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
    95	
    96	## Consumer invocation pattern
    97	
    98	```bash
    99	# Direct call — no shim.
   100	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py" ship pr [args...]
   101	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py" report-tokens analyze [args...]
   102	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/python/cli.py" lint retired-scripts [args...]

   106	domain module (lazy import).

    12	#   DIRS_SLIMMED=<N>    Dirs slimmed (non-delete mode).
    13	#   DIRS_DELETED=<N>    Dirs fully deleted (--delete mode).
    14	#   DIRS_SKIPPED=<N>    Dirs skipped (guard matched, or already slimmed).
    15	#   BYTES_FREED=<N>     Approximate bytes freed (0 in dry-run).
    16	#   DRY_RUN=true|false

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# status.sh — larch version and vendor health status check.
     3	#
     4	# Outputs (KEY=value on stdout via emit_kv):
     5	#   LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION=<value>   Current larch plugin version.
     6	#   CODEX_BINARY_FOUND=true|false  Whether the codex binary is on PATH.
     7	#   CURSOR_BINARY_FOUND=true|false Whether the cursor binary is on PATH.

    10	#   CODEX_STATE=ok|binary-missing|probe-failed
    11	#   CURSOR_STATE=ok|binary-missing|probe-failed
    12	#   DEGRADED=true|false            Whether any vendor is unavailable.
    13	
    14	set -euo pipefail
    15	
    16	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
    17	PLUGIN_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd -P)}"
    18	# shellcheck source=scripts/lib-quiet.sh
    19	source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib-quiet.sh"
    20	larch_quiet_init

    22	# Read plugin version (best-effort; always emits a value)
    23	LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION="unknown"
    24	_ver_out=$(python3 "$PLUGIN_ROOT/python/cli.py" plugin read-version 2>/dev/null || true)
    25	if [ -n "$_ver_out" ]; then
    26	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_ver_out" | awk -F= '/^LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    27	    [ -n "$_v" ] && LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION="$_v"
    28	fi

    30	# Run reviewer health probes (same machinery as /implement Step 0)
    31	CODEX_BINARY_FOUND=false
    32	CURSOR_BINARY_FOUND=false
    33	CODEX_PRESENT=false
    34	CURSOR_PRESENT=false
    35	_check_out=$(python3 "$PLUGIN_ROOT/python/cli.py" agent check-reviewers 2>/dev/null || true)
    36	if [ -n "$_check_out" ]; then
    37	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_check_out" | awk -F= '/^CODEX_BINARY_FOUND=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    38	    [ -n "$_v" ] && CODEX_BINARY_FOUND="$_v"
    39	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_check_out" | awk -F= '/^CURSOR_BINARY_FOUND=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    40	    [ -n "$_v" ] && CURSOR_BINARY_FOUND="$_v"
    41	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_check_out" | awk -F= '/^CODEX_PRESENT=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    42	    [ -n "$_v" ] && CODEX_PRESENT="$_v"
    43	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_check_out" | awk -F= '/^CURSOR_PRESENT=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    44	    [ -n "$_v" ] && CURSOR_PRESENT="$_v"
    45	fi
    46	
    47	# Interpret results using agent degraded-tools-gate (same gate as /implement Step 0)
    48	CODEX_STATE=unknown
    49	CURSOR_STATE=unknown
    50	DEGRADED=false
    51	_gate_out=$(python3 "$PLUGIN_ROOT/python/cli.py" agent degraded-tools-gate \
    52	    --codex-binary-found "$CODEX_BINARY_FOUND" \

    54	    --cursor-binary-found "$CURSOR_BINARY_FOUND" \

    61	    [ -n "$_v" ] && CURSOR_STATE="$_v"
    62	    _v=$(printf '%s\n' "$_gate_out" | awk -F= '/^DEGRADED=/{print substr($0, index($0,"=")+1); exit}')
    63	    [ -n "$_v" ] && DEGRADED="$_v"

Validator failure is rewritten to `STATUS=NOT_SUBSTANTIVE`, and the caller treats it identically to a timeout (Claude-subagent fallback). This catches outputs that pass sentinel + non-empty + retry but contain only banner text (e.g., `Authentication required`) or other non-substantive content.

    65	def flowchart_rejects_pipe(line: str) -> bool:
    66	    """Port sanitize-mermaid-fragment.sh flowchart_reject (depth + quote aware)."""
    67	    depth = 0
    68	    quote = False
    69	    esc = False
    70	    for char in line:
    71	        if depth > 0 and quote:
    72	            if esc:
    73	                esc = False
    74	            elif char == "\\":
    75	                esc = True
    76	            elif char == '"':
    77	                quote = False
    78	            continue
    79	        if depth > 0 and char == '"':
    80	            quote = True
    81	            continue
    82	        if char in _OPEN_BRACKET:
    83	            depth += 1
    84	            continue
    85	        if depth > 0 and char in _CLOSE_BRACKET:
    86	            depth -= 1
    87	            continue
    88	        if depth > 0 and char == "|":
    89	            return True
    90	    return False

     2	# compose-pr-summary.sh — emit 1-3 Markdown summary bullets for the PR body.
     3	
     4	set -euo pipefail

     6	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    10	
    11	usage() {
    12	    while IFS= read -r line; do larch_err "$line"; done <<'USAGE'
    13	Usage:
    14	  compose-pr-summary.sh --plan-goals-file PATH
    15	USAGE
    16	}

    20	    exit 2
    21	}
    22	
    23	PLAN_GOALS_FILE=""

    25	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    26	    case "$1" in
    27	        --plan-goals-file)
    28	            PLAN_GOALS_FILE="${2:?--plan-goals-file requires a value}"
    29	            shift 2
    30	            ;;
    31	        -h|--help)
    32	            usage
    33	            exit 0
    34	            ;;
    35	        *)
    36	            usage
    37	            fail "unknown option: $1"
    38	            ;;
    39	    esac
    40	done
    41	
    42	[ -n "$PLAN_GOALS_FILE" ] || { usage; fail "--plan-goals-file is required"; }
    43	if ! [ -f "$PLAN_GOALS_FILE" ] || ! [ -s "$PLAN_GOALS_FILE" ]; then
    44	    fail "plan-goals file missing or empty: $PLAN_GOALS_FILE"
    45	fi
    46	
    47	# Bullet 1: first non-blank line of the ## Goal section (stop at next heading).
    48	goal_line=$(awk '/^## Goal/{found=1; next} found && /^#/{exit} found && NF{print; exit}' "$PLAN_GOALS_FILE")
    49	[ -n "$goal_line" ] || fail "no Goal line found in $PLAN_GOALS_FILE"
    50	
    51	summary=$(printf -- '- %s\n' "$goal_line")
    52	
    53	# Derive changed-file list against merge-base.
    54	merge_base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null) || merge_base=""
    55	changed_files=""
    56	if [ -n "$merge_base" ]; then
    57	    changed_files=$(git diff --name-only "$merge_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null) || changed_files=""
    58	fi
    59	
    60	# Bullet 2: test files changed.
    61	if [ -n "$changed_files" ]; then
    62	    test_count=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | grep -cE '(^|/)test-[^/]+\.sh$' || true)
    63	    if [ "${test_count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    64	        summary="$summary"$'\n'"$(printf -- '- Added or updated %s test file(s).' "$test_count")"
    65	    fi
    66	fi
    67	
    68	# Bullet 3: cross-cutting changes (>2 distinct top-level dirs).
    69	if [ -n "$changed_files" ]; then
    70	    dir_count=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | awk -F/ 'NF>1{print $1} NF==1{print "."}' | sort -u | grep -c '.' || true)

    72	        cross_dirs=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed_files" | awk -F/ 'NF>1{print $1} NF==1{print "."}' | sort -u | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')

This is a fail-closed documentation requirement for any future summary-warning callsites: if a helper persists tool stderr into execution-issues or a public-boundary artifact, it must route through the shared redaction pipeline first.

    49	6. **Delete bash script + harness + `.md` siblings** — remove the old
    50	   `.sh`, `.md`, and test harness files. Do not leave stubs.
    51	
    52	7. **Append to manifest** — add the deleted paths to `python/migrated-scripts.tsv`
    53	   (full repo-relative path in column 1, `#<issue>` in column 2). This is how
    54	   `make lint-retired-scripts` knows what to check for lingering references.
    55	
    56	8. **`make lint-retired-scripts`** — run (or let CI run) `make lint-retired-scripts`
    57	   to confirm no tracked file still references any of the retired paths.
    58	
    59	## Manifest format
    60	
    61	`python/migrated-scripts.tsv` — tab-separated, `path<TAB>retired_by`:
    62	
    63	```
    64	# Retired script manifest for the sh-to-py migration.
    65	# Format: path<TAB>retired_by
    66	scripts/old-helper.sh    #1234
    67	```
    68	
    69	Rules:
    70	
    71	- **Path-precise references plus scoped dev-skill basenames.** The linter matches
    72	  the full repo-relative manifest path everywhere and same-directory
    73	  `$SCRIPT_DIR/<basename>.sh` / `${SCRIPT_DIR}/<basename>.sh` forms derived from
    74	  that manifest path. It also matches bare basenames only in same-directory
    75	  `.claude/skills/**/*.md` dev-skill docs when no live sibling `.sh` exists.
    76	  Repo-wide bare basenames outside that scoped branch are not matched, so a live
    77	  file at `other/path/run-analysis.sh` will not be flagged for a retired path at
    78	  `scripts/old/run-analysis.sh`.
    79	- Retired path references are deletion blockers whenever they match the manifest
    80	  path or same-directory invocation forms. Comment and prose references are
    81	  scanned the same way as code unless they fall under the exclusions below.
    82	- Exclusions from scanning: any file under a `larch-logs/` path segment,
    83	  `CHANGELOG.md`, and the manifest file itself are never scanned.
    84	- **Do NOT write retired-path literals in test fixtures.** Build fixture paths
    85	  programmatically at runtime so tests remain valid if the manifest changes.
